648-for contextuality (neither logical nor strong) even under reasonably strong assumptions on symmetry and
649-connectedness of the cover, and, although obstructions can be generalised to higher cohomology groups,
650-they cannot be applied to the study of no-signalling empirical models. In future work, we aim to re-
651-develop the sheaf-cohomological study of contextuality from a different viewpoint. The machinery of
652-obstruction theory, a branch of homotopy theory that deals with the extendability of maps, allows the def-
653-inition of obstructions to the extension of continuous functions in a cohomology theory with coefficients
654-in the homotopy groups. This promising approach will require an adaptation of the concept of empiri-
655-cal model to fit this framework. A possibility would be to formalise the bundle diagram representation
656-and define models as fiber bundles or, more generally, as fibrations. This would allow the definition of
657-Postnikov towers [26], which give rise to cohomological obstructions.
658-
659-    In the last section, we have provided an alternative description of the first cohomology group using
660:torsors relative to a presheaf. Although this approach is still at a developing stage, it allows us to un-
661-derstand cohomological obstructions as a concrete mathematical object. The implications of this new
662-viewpoint will be considered in future work.

-Assume $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ is admitted at $p$, write $a=[r]_p$, and let $S_e$ be the support presheaf of a finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model. If
+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here.  Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}.  More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}.  Neither construction produces a banded gerbe

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model (e), the following sets are naturally
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
+      (s_C\in S_e(C));
+\item global assignments (s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x) such that
+      (s|_C\in S_e(C)) for every (C\in\mathcal M);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both (\CompSec_s(r)) and (\Sec_s(r)) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
 \[
-M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-S_e\ \text{has a global section}.
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
 \]
-\end{enumerate}
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
 
 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.
 
-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. +The empirical-model interface gives a sharp limit to this canonicity.  \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} proves that every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical split realization-stack extension, pseudonatural under ordinary refinements of measurement contexts, but every component gerbe in that extension is neutral.  The Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa class is a relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ class, equivalently a torsor class \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}; it is indexed by a chosen local section.  By contrast, the Giraud map here is an $H^2$ class indexed by a global component, and for a strongly contextual model that indexing set is empty.     1: \subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}

    3: Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
    4: reformulations close to the question considered here.  Car\`u identifies the
    5: degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
    6: trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}.  More recently,
    7: Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
    8: scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
    9: isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
   10: \cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}.  Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
   11: or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
   12: \Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}.  The following comparison locates the
   13: gap precisely.

   15: Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set (X), finite
   16: nonempty outcome sets (O_x) for (x\in X), and a finite antichain
   17: \(\mathcal M\) of subsets of (X) whose union is (X).  Write
   18: \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
   19: the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
   20: equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts.  We also use its
   21: terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining (X) and declaring
   22: \(\mathcal M\) to cover (X).  A finite empirical model
   23: \[
   24: e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
   25: \]
   26: is a compatible family of probability distributions on
   27: \(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\).  Its support presheaf is
   28: \[
   29: S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
   30: \qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
   31: \]
   32: where compatibility makes the marginal (e_U) independent of the maximal
   33: context containing (U) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}.  At the adjoined
   34: terminal object we take the right Kan extension
   35: \[
   36: \widehat S_e(X):=
   37: \varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
   38: \]
   39: Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
   40: of supported local assignments.
   41: 
   42: A \emph{context refinement} used below is a refinement
   43: \(\rho:\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\) on the same measurements and outcomes,
   44: with (C'\subseteq\rho(C')), for which marginalization defines the refined
   45: model \(\rho^*e\).  It induces the usual morphism of finite context sites
   46: \(u_\rho\) and a natural base-change isomorphism
   47: \[
   48: S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e.
   49: \]
   50: This includes ordinary iterated refinements of the measurement cover.  No
   51: claim is made here for resource-theoretic simulations which change the
   52: measurement or outcome sets.

   54: \begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
   55: For every finite empirical model (e), the following sets are naturally
   56: bijection:
   57: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   58: \item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
   59:       (s_C\in S_e(C));
   60: \item global assignments (s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x) such that
   61:       (s|_C\in S_e(C)) for every (C\in\mathcal M);
   62: \item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
   63:       Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
   64: \item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
   65:       \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
   66: \end{enumerate}
   67: Consequently, if both (\CompSec_s(r)) and (\Sec_s(r)) are interpreted
   68: from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
   69: \[
   70: M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
   71: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   72: M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
   73: \]
   74: In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
   75: set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
   76: \(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
   77: \end{proposition}
   78: 
   79: \begin{proof}
   80: The event presheaf
   81: \(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf.  Hence a compatible family
   82: \((s_C)\) glues uniquely to a global assignment (s\), and its restrictions
   83: remain in the prescribed supports.  Conversely, restriction of such an
   84: assignment gives a compatible supported family.  This proves the first three
   85: identifications.  The fourth is the defining limit formula for
   86: \(\widehat S_e(X)\); the plus construction for the cover
   87: \(\mathcal M\to X\) gives the same set in the sheafification.  The displayed
   88: equivalence follows immediately.
   89: \end{proof}

   91: \begin{theorem}[Canonical split stack and the degree obstruction]\label{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}
   92: Let (e) be a finite empirical model on the context site above.
   93: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   94: \item There is a canonical realization-stack extension with zero band,
   95: \[
   96: \mathfrak E_e^0:=\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e),
   97: \qquad
   98: \pi_0(\mathfrak E_e^0)\cong aS_e.
   99: \]
  100: Here \(\operatorname{Disc}\) regards a sheaf of sets as a stack of discrete
  101: groupoids.
  102: \item More generally, after an abelian sheaf \(\Band\) has been supplied,
  103: there is a canonical split \(\Band\)-banded extension
  104: \[
  105: \mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}:=
  106: \operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\Band.
  107: \]
  108: Every component gerbe of this extension is neutral, and therefore every
  109: Giraud class supplied by
  110: \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is zero.
  111: \item The assignments in \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are pseudonatural
  112: under context refinements: there are coherent banded equivalences
  113: \[
  114: u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^0\simeq
  115: \mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^0,
  116: \qquad
  117: u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}\simeq
  118: \mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^{\mathrm{spl}}
  119: \]
  120: in the second formula whenever the supplied bands are identified under
  121: pullback.
  122: \item The bare empirical model does not canonically produce the non-split
  123: degree-two data required by this paper.  More precisely, fix
  124: \(C_0\in\mathcal M\) and (s\in S_e(C_0)).  Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa
  125: form the free-abelian presheaf
  126: \(\mathcal F_e=\mathbb Z[S_e]\), its relative kernel
  127: \(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\), and a class
  128: \[
  129: \gamma_e(s)\in
  130: \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}).
  131: \]
  132: This class is the isomorphism class of an
  133: \(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\)-torsor trivialized by
  134: \(\mathcal M\), not a Giraud class of a banded gerbe
  135: \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}.
  136: \item There is no comparison which recovers these AMB classes, for all finite
  137: empirical models, from the branch map of any realization-stack extension
  138: whose component sheaf is (aS_e).  Indeed, if (e) is strongly contextual,
  139: then
  140: \[
  141: (aS_e)(X)=\varnothing,
  142: \]
  143: so the branch map
  144: \[
  145: \delta_{\mathfrak E_e}:(aS_e)(X)longrightarrow
  146: H^2(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M},\Band)
  147: \]
  148: has empty domain, whereas AMB classes are defined for the local sections
  149: \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) and can be nonzero, as in their GHZ and
  150: Kochen--Specker examples.
  151: \end{enumerate}
  152: In \textup{(i)}, ``canonical'' means that the construction is the composite
  153: of the universal sheafification functor and the discrete-stack functor, with
  154: no choices, and that the displayed refinement equivalences satisfy the usual
  155: pseudofunctor coherence.  It does not mean that all realization-stack
  156: extensions of (S_e) are equivalent.
  157: \end{theorem}
  158: 
  159: \begin{proof}
  160: The discrete groupoid construction preserves descent, so
  161: \(\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\) is a stack and its connected-component sheaf is
  162: exactly (aS_e).  Its automorphism sheaves are zero, proving \textup{(i)}.
  163: The classifying stack \(\mathsf B\Band\) has one local component and
  164: automorphism sheaf \(\Band\).  Taking its product with the discrete stack
  165: therefore proves the band and component assertions in \textup{(ii)}.  The
  166: global object represented by the identity \(\Band\)-torsor neutralizes each
  167: component gerbe, so its Giraud class vanishes.
  168: 
  169: Inverse image for the morphism of context sites commutes, up to its canonical
  170: isomorphism, with associated sheaves, discrete stacks, products, and
  171: classifying stacks.  Together with
  172: \(S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e\), this gives the equivalences and their
  173: coherence in \textup{(iii)}.
  174: 
  175: The construction of \(\gamma_e(s)\) and its degree are those of
  176: \cite[Sec.~4]{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}.  The torsor
  177: classification is \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}, proving \textup{(iv)}.  Finally,
  178: \Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation} identifies strong contextuality with
  179: emptiness of \((aS_e)(X)\).  The branch obstruction map of
  180: \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is indexed by precisely
  181: that set, while \(\gamma_e(s)\) is indexed by a local section.  This proves
  182: the asserted failure in \textup{(v)}.
  183: \end{proof}
  184: 
  185: \begin{corollary}[Exact limit of transfer to empirical models]\label{thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}
  186: For finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models, the set-valued
  187: local-to-global statements of \Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
  188: transfer functorially.  The later banded and homological theorems transfer
  189: only after a band and a non-split realization-stack extension have been
  190: supplied as additional data.  In particular:
  191: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  192: \item the canonical split extension gives only zero Giraud classes and zero
  193: hidden subgroups;
  194: \item the characterization
  195: \[
  196: d(G)\le 2\beta
  197: \quad\text{and}\quad
  198: G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}
  199: \]
  200: remains a realization theorem for the chosen bouquet good-cover, band, and
  201: two-branch cocycle data of
  202: \Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution}; it is not a characterization of
  203: groups canonically attached to empirical models;
  204: \item without an additional degree-shifting construction, the Giraud
  205: \(H^2\)-class neither recovers nor refines the AMB relative
  206: \(\check H^1\)-obstruction.
  207: \end{enumerate}
  208: \end{corollary}
  209: 
  210: \begin{proof}
  211: The first and third assertions are
  212: \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}(ii),(iv)--(v).  The bouquet theorem
  213: starts from a prescribed finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and
  214: chosen branchwise homomorphisms
  215: \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\).  None of those data is selected by a bare empirical
  216: model, so its group classification cannot be transported through the split
  217: construction.  This proves the second assertion.
  218: \end{proof}

  348: \section{A conditional GHZ/Mermin amplitude-lift template}\label{sec:appendix-ghz}
  349: 
  350: The GHZ/Mermin model provides a convenient illustration of the extra
  351: realization data needed before the conditional gerbe machinery becomes
  352: available. The role of this section is correspondingly limited: it is a
  353: conditional template for chosen amplitude-lift data, not a constructed
  354: finite-nerve GHZ example. In particular, it does not supply a canonical
  355: finite nerve, a normalized cocycle, a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison map, a
  356: global-conservativity proof, or a canonical value of $K_\omega$ for GHZ.
  357: 
  358: Let $e_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model obtained from the GHZ state \cite{GreenbergerHorneZeilinger1989,Mermin1990,AbramskyBrandenburger2011}, situated in the Kochen--Specker tradition \cite{KochenSpecker1967}. Related topological and cohomological treatments of contextuality include \cite{OkayRaussendorf2016,OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017,OkayTyhurstRaussendorf2018,Aasnaess2022}. The measurement cover consists of the four contexts
  359: \[
  360: C_{XXX},\ C_{XYY},\ C_{YXY},\ C_{YYX},
  361: \]
  362: where, for instance, $C_{XYY}$ records the joint measurement in which the first observer measures $X$ and the other two measure $Y$. Each context carries outcomes in $\{\pm 1\}^3$, and the GHZ support presheaf $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ selects exactly the assignments whose parity matches the GHZ constraints: $+1$ on $XXX$ and $-1$ on the three $XYY$-type contexts.
  363: 
  364: \begin{definition}[Amplitude lift of a support presheaf]\label{def:amplitude-lift}
  365: Let $S_e$ be the support presheaf of a finite empirical model on a measurement-cover site $\mathcal C_a$. An \emph{amplitude lift} of $S_e$ with band $\Band$ is a realization prestack
  366: \[
  367: \mathfrak P_e\to \mathcal C_a
  368: \]
  369: together with an identification
  370: \[
  371: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_e)\cong S_e.
  372: \]
  373: Equivalently, an amplitude lift is a choice of local realization objects and phase-sensitive transition isomorphisms whose isomorphism classes recover the supported local assignments.
  374: \end{definition}
  375: 
  376: \begin{remark}[Support data versus amplitude data]\label{rem:amplitude-lift-choice}
  377: The support presheaf records only which local assignments are allowed. It does not determine an amplitude lift, a branch gerbe, a derived branch class, or a value of $K_\omega$. All gerbe-theoretic claims for empirical support presheaves are therefore relative to a chosen lift.
  378: \end{remark}
  379: 
  380: \begin{lemma}[Chosen GHZ phase-line lift]\label{lem:ghz-prestack}
  381: Let $a=[r]_p$ be the GHZ reference class and $\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. Fix, for each object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and each supported local assignment $s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$, a one-dimensional complex line $L_{U,s}$ generated by a chosen local GHZ amplitude, together with restriction isomorphisms compatible with restriction of assignments. Let $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$ be the groupoid whose objects are the pairs
  382: \[
  383: (s,L_{U,s}),
  384: \qquad
  385: s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U),
  386: \]
  387: and whose automorphisms are the signs $\{\pm 1\}\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ acting on the chosen line. Then $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}\to\mathcal C_a$ is an amplitude lift of $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ with band $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$.
  388: \end{lemma}
  389: 
  390: \begin{proof}
  391: By construction, restriction along $V\to U$ sends $(s,L_{U,s})$ to the restricted supported assignment together with the chosen restricted line, so the fibres form a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C_a$. The automorphism sheaf of every object is the constant sheaf $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, acting by sign changes on the one-dimensional line. Forgetting the line remembers only the supported assignment, and two objects are isomorphic exactly when they have the same supported assignment. Hence
  392: \[
  393: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})\cong S_{\mathrm{GHZ}},
  394: \]
  395: so \Cref{def:amplitude-lift} is satisfied.
  396: \end{proof}
  397: 
  398: \begin{theorem}[Conditional GHZ/Mermin realization template]\label{thm:ghz-realization}
  399: Let $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the GHZ support presheaf, and fix the chosen amplitude lift $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ of \Cref{lem:ghz-prestack}. Suppose, in addition, that one has chosen a stackification
  400: \[
  401: \mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}}:=a(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})
  402: \]
  403: and a cofinal family of covers
  404: \[
  405: \Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)
  406: \]
  407: such that the global-conservativity and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison clauses of \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization} hold for this chosen lift. Then
  408: \[
  409: (\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}})
  410: \]
  411: is a gluing-sensitive realization datum for the chosen GHZ amplitude lift, and the conditional gerbe semantics of \Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition,thm:gerbe-null-semantics} applies to it when the associated reference slice is slice-separated. No claim is made that the bare support presheaf canonically determines a finite nerve presentation, a derived branch class, or a specific value of $K_\omega$.
  412: \end{theorem}
  413: 
  414: \begin{proof}
  415: \Cref{lem:ghz-prestack} provides the extra amplitude data absent from the support presheaf itself. The additional assumptions are exactly the remaining clauses in \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}. Once those data are fixed, the general theorems of the main text apply verbatim.
  416: \end{proof}
The Editors
Annals of Pure and Applied Logic

Dear Editors,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript "Gluing Obstructions
and Homological Visibility in a State-Forcing Semantics."  The paper
addresses the following question: given a presheaf carrying a finite
abelian gluing obstruction, what part of that obstruction is
semantically visible -- that is, detectable by admissible characters --
without enlarging the state space?

The answer is developed within a four-layer conservative extension
chain that stratifies the passage from pointwise semantics through
information-state forcing to local objects and refinement dynamics.
Each layer strictly extends the one below and preserves the forcing
behavior of all formulas already expressible at lower layers.  The
first main result (Theorem A) is a forcing-necessity separation
theorem: compatible local sectionability and gluing-level absence are
undefinable in the information-state forcing language, so the
local-object enrichment is logically necessary.  The second result
(Theorem B) establishes a branched gerbe semantics in which each
visible value class determines a banded component gerbe, and
gluing-level absence holds exactly when every component gerbe is
non-neutral.  The third result (Theorem C) applies the universal
coefficient theorem to define the intrinsic visible quotient as the
cokernel of a homological evaluation map; the blind residual -- the
part of the obstruction invisible to every admissible character -- is a
pure Ext-type class.  In the unique-branch support-presheaf setting,
this recovers the Abramsky--Brandenburger no-global-section picture and
identifies the precise mechanism behind cohomological blind cases.

APAL is our preferred venue because the paper draws on several
traditions that the journal has helped develop.  The conservative
extension chain builds on Kripke's semantics for intuitionistic logic,
Beth's semantic tableaux, and Fitting's model-theoretic forcing.  The
gerbe-theoretic layer applies the Giraud classification in a
site-specific way that connects to the topos-theoretic forcing of
Tierney and Johnstone; we discuss the relationship explicitly in the
conclusion, including the open question of whether the four-layer chain
admits a topos-internal reformulation via Lawvere--Tierney topologies.
The combination of Heyting-valued forcing separation with homological
algebra over finite Cech nerves lies squarely within the journal's
scope in categorical logic and sheaf-theoretic methods.

The manuscript is 92 pages in amsart format, contains
38 references, and is self-contained: all definitions, hypotheses, and
proofs are given in full.  No external data or computational
verification is required.  Results on multi-observer extensions are
deferred to a sequel and are not needed for the present paper.

Thank you for considering this submission.

Sincerely,
The Authors

For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. +The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
 
 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}
 
 \keywords{state forcing, local objects, sheafification, gerbes, visible quotient, universal coefficient theorem}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
+\item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
 \[
-M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-S_e\ \text{has a global section}.
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
 \]
-\end{enumerate}
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
+\item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
 \end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
+\[
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
+\]
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

+The event presheaf
+\(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf. Hence a compatible family

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}
 
 \keywords{state forcing, local objects, sheafification, gerbes, visible quotient, universal coefficient theorem}

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}
 
 \keywords{state forcing, local objects, sheafification, gerbes, visible quotient, universal coefficient theorem}

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}
 
 \keywords{state forcing, local objects, sheafification, gerbes, visible quotient, universal coefficient theorem}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]

+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);

+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);

+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations.  The paper separates three stages of the local-to-global problem. At the level of information states, \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} shows that compatible local sectionability and gluing-level nullity are invisible in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment considered here. This is not intended as a general expressivity theorem, but it does isolate the first place at which the local-object layer goes beyond the lower forcing language.
 
-At the passage from set-valued to groupoid-valued data, \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} shows that a slice-separated representative-rigid lift can be globally conservative only when the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre is surjective; under $H^1$-vanishing and slice-separatedness on the reference slice, this is equivalent to sheafiness of the local object functor at that fibre. Thus the gerbe-theoretic part of the theory is necessarily relative to additional lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the maximal canonicity available without an existence theorem: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction class is intrinsic up to equivalence of such extensions. Visible value classes are then governed by the sheaf of connected components; on slice-separated reference slices, strict gluing failure is carried by the component gerbes of the visible branches.

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section.  \end{abstract}

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution.  The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable.
