+Under the same fixed finite-nerve, constant-band, $H_1=0$, and mixed-realization hypotheses, if $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta$, \Cref{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification} shows that the realizable hidden subgroups are exactly the subgroups of $A$ generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The bouquet theorem \Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution} then supplies an explicit chosen family of examples, namely open-star good covers of a fixed finite model of $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, for which the acyclic-cover hypothesis is automatic and the pure two-branch resolution kernels can be classified explicitly: a finite abelian group $G$ occurs precisely when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. This is an existence and classification statement inside the chosen good-cover construction, not a uniqueness assertion for all presentations of the bouquet and, by \Cref{thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}, not an invariant canonically attached to empirical models.
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the dependence on extra realization data is made explicit, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant at fixed finite nerve presentations, with functorial transport along chosen finite comparison zigzags inside the controlled finite-nerve comparison groupoid.
+The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
 
 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain

+\[

+\[

  313: \subsection{Lower-fragment separation}
  314: 
  315: The three null modes show that information-state forcing distinguishes situations invisible to pointwise semantics. By \Cref{prop:chain-instantiation}, the reference sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ already belongs to the $\Sigma_1$-signature, whereas the predicates
  316: \[
  317: \Adm_s,\qquad \LocSec_s,\qquad \CompSec_s,\qquad \Sec_s
  318: \]
  319: belong to $\Sigma_2\setminus\Sigma_1$. The lower layer can therefore quantify over reference elements but cannot mention the local-object predicates themselves. To keep track of the formulas allowed in that comparison, we fix the following terminology.
  320: 
  321: \begin{definition}[Automorphism-invariant lower comparison class]\label{def:lower-comparison-class}
  322: Let $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The automorphism-invariant lower comparison class $\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ consists of the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-formulas with exactly one free variable of sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$, no parameters of that sort, and any number of bound variables from the ambient pointwise signature. A formula $\varphi(x)\in\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ is evaluated inside the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-reduct of an $\mathbb L_1$-model, and it is required to be invariant under automorphisms of that reduct.
  323: \end{definition}
  324: 
  325: \begin{definition}[Gluing-sensitive realization datum]\label{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}
  326: Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$ and write $a=[r]_p$. A \emph{gluing-sensitive realization datum} for $r$ is a tuple
  327: \[
  328: (\mathfrak P_r,\mathfrak L_r,\Band,\Cov_r^{\mathrm{acyc}})
  329: \]
  330: with the following properties:
  331: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  332: \item $\mathfrak P_r\to\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$ is a realization prestack with band $\Band$ in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack};
  333: \item $\mathfrak L_r$ is a $\Band$-banded stack whose connected components agree with the sheafification of $F_{p,s}$, i.e.
  334: \[
  335: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a};
  336: \]
  337: \item the stackification morphism $\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to\mathfrak L_r$ is globally conservative at $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity};
  338: \item for each visible branch supported by the datum, the induced family
  339: \(\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\) is part of a \v{C}ech--derived comparison
  340: package in the sense of \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}; in
  341: particular, its covers admit \v{C}ech nerves in the slice, trivialize the
  342: band where the obstruction cocycles are computed, and carry the specified
  343: comparison isomorphism to derived cohomology.
  344: \end{enumerate}
  345: If such a datum exists we say that $r$ admits a gluing-sensitive realization. This datum is extra structure on top of the bare local object functor: later sections treat the gerbe-theoretic layer only relative to a chosen datum of this kind and do not assert that every local object functor admits one.
  346: \end{definition}

  313: \subsection{Lower-fragment separation}
  314: 
  315: The three null modes show that information-state forcing distinguishes situations invisible to pointwise semantics. By \Cref{prop:chain-instantiation}, the reference sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ already belongs to the $\Sigma_1$-signature, whereas the predicates
  316: \[
  317: \Adm_s,\qquad \LocSec_s,\qquad \CompSec_s,\qquad \Sec_s
  318: \]
  319: belong to $\Sigma_2\setminus\Sigma_1$. The lower layer can therefore quantify over reference elements but cannot mention the local-object predicates themselves. To keep track of the formulas allowed in that comparison, we fix the following terminology.
  320: 
  321: \begin{definition}[Automorphism-invariant lower comparison class]\label{def:lower-comparison-class}
  322: Let $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The automorphism-invariant lower comparison class $\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ consists of the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-formulas with exactly one free variable of sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$, no parameters of that sort, and any number of bound variables from the ambient pointwise signature. A formula $\varphi(x)\in\mathcal{C}_{s}^{\mathrm{inv}}$ is evaluated inside the constant-free $\Sigma_1$-reduct of an $\mathbb L_1$-model, and it is required to be invariant under automorphisms of that reduct.
  323: \end{definition}
  324: 
  325: \begin{definition}[Gluing-sensitive realization datum]\label{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}
  326: Fix an admitted reference $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$ and write $a=[r]_p$. A \emph{gluing-sensitive realization datum} for $r$ is a tuple
  327: \[
  328: (\mathfrak P_r,\mathfrak L_r,\Band,\Cov_r^{\mathrm{acyc}})
  329: \]
  330: with the following properties:
  331: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  332: \item $\mathfrak P_r\to\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$ is a realization prestack with band $\Band$ in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack};
  333: \item $\mathfrak L_r$ is a $\Band$-banded stack whose connected components agree with the sheafification of $F_{p,s}$, i.e.
  334: \[
  335: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a};
  336: \]
  337: \item the stackification morphism $\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to\mathfrak L_r$ is globally conservative at $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity};
  338: \item for each visible branch supported by the datum, the induced family
  339: \(\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\) is part of a \v{C}ech--derived comparison
  340: package in the sense of \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}; in
  341: particular, its covers admit \v{C}ech nerves in the slice, trivialize the
  342: band where the obstruction cocycles are computed, and carry the specified
  343: comparison isomorphism to derived cohomology.
  344: \end{enumerate}
  345: If such a datum exists we say that $r$ admits a gluing-sensitive realization. This datum is extra structure on top of the bare local object functor: later sections treat the gerbe-theoretic layer only relative to a chosen datum of this kind and do not assert that every local object functor admits one.
  346: \end{definition}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\[

+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)

+\]

+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[

+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.
 
-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes. +The empirical-model interface gives a sharp limit to this canonicity.  \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} proves that every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical split realization-stack extension, pseudonatural under ordinary refinements of measurement contexts, but every component gerbe in that extension is neutral.  The Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa class is a relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ class of a presheaf, equivalently a torsor class \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}; it is indexed by a chosen local section.  The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations.  The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors

+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the

+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring

+\[

+\]

+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)

 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}
+
+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. +We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. +\subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}
+
+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the

+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement

+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)

+\]

+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
+Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
+scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
+\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]
+where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
+context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
+\]
+Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
+of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
+this terminally augmented presheaf.

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. +Under the same fixed finite-nerve, constant-band, $H_1=0$, and mixed-realization hypotheses, if $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta$, \Cref{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification} shows that the realizable hidden subgroups are exactly the subgroups of $A$ generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The bouquet theorem \Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution} then supplies an explicit chosen family of examples, namely open-star good covers of a fixed finite model of $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, for which the acyclic-cover hypothesis is automatic and the pure two-branch resolution kernels can be classified explicitly: a finite abelian group $G$ occurs precisely when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. This is an existence and classification statement inside the chosen good-cover construction, not a uniqueness assertion for all presentations of the bouquet and, by \Cref{thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}, not an invariant canonically attached to empirical models.
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the dependence on extra realization data is made explicit, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant at fixed finite nerve presentations, with functorial transport along chosen finite comparison zigzags inside the controlled finite-nerve comparison groupoid.
+The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed.  The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. +We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors

+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.
+
+Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
+nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
+\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
+\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
+the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
+equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
+terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
+\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
+\[
+e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
+\]
+is a compatible family of probability distributions on
+\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
+\[
+S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
+\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
+\]

+terminal object we take the right Kan extension
+\[
+\widehat S_e(X):=
+\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. +The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed.  The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. +We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
 
 The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}

 The paper separates three stages of the local-to-global problem. At the level of information states, \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} shows that compatible local sectionability and gluing-level nullity are invisible in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment considered here. This is not intended as a general expressivity theorem, but it does isolate the first place at which the local-object layer goes beyond the lower forcing language.

 The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. +The empirical-model interface gives a sharp limit to this canonicity.  \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} proves that every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical split realization-stack extension, pseudonatural under ordinary refinements of measurement contexts, but every component gerbe in that extension is neutral.  The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.  \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. +We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. +\subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}

+Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
+reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
+degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
+trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,

+or a realization-stack extension in the sense of
+\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
+gap precisely.

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
+\item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
 \end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
+\[
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
+\]
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

+\begin{remark}[Support versus probabilistic contextuality]\label{rem:support-vs-probabilistic-contextuality}
+The proposition concerns the possibilistic support of \(e\). Probabilistic
+noncontextuality asks instead for a distribution on
+\(\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) whose marginals are the given distributions \(e_C\).
+That is a fibre-extension problem for the distribution presheaf, and is not
+determined by \(S_e\): empirical models with the same support can have
+different probabilistic noncontextuality behaviour.
+\end{remark}
