 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]

+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);

+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
 \end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
+\[
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
+\]
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
+For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
+bijection:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
+      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
+\item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
+      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
+\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
+      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
+\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
+      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
 \end{enumerate}
+Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
+from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
+\[
+M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
+\]
+In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
+set-valued level; it is not the gluing-level mode
+\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
 \end{proposition}

+\begin{remark}[Support versus probabilistic contextuality]\label{rem:support-vs-probabilistic-contextuality}
+The proposition concerns the possibilistic support of \(e\). Probabilistic
+noncontextuality asks instead for a distribution on
+\(\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) whose marginals are the given distributions \(e_C\).

 No required in-scope theorem from the scope contract is completely absent from the compiled manuscript. The main risks are not missing labels but proof-interface sharpness and source hygiene:
 

codex
**Literature**

No existing bridge from finite Abramsky–Brandenburger empirical models to banded realization stacks or gerbes was found in arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or zbMATH. Semantic Scholar’s final bulk searches returned zero results for `contextuality gerbe`, `empirical model gerbe`, and `banded gerbe contextuality`.

The closest results are materially different:

- Carù proves that AMB’s first cohomology classes classify torsors trivialized by the measurement cover.
- Barbosa–Kharoof–Okay construct fully faithful, empirical-model-compatible functors into bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios.
- Neither construction produces a sheaf-banded gerbe, a Giraud \(H^2\)-class, or this paper’s realization-stack extension. The previously recorded bundle citation was incorrect and has been corrected in [references.bib](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/references.bib:347).

**Precise Result**

[sec_branch_contextuality.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/sec_branch_contextuality.tex:1) now treats finite no-signalling empirical models on the terminal augmentation of the finite context site. For context refinements whose context inclusion is continuous and satisfies support base change, it proves the pseudonatural assignment
\[
\mathfrak E_e^0=\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)
\]
with canonical zero band. After separately supplying an abelian sheaf \(\mathscr A\), it gives the split extension
\[
\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\mathscr A .
\]
“Canonical” means the choice-free composite of sheafification and the discrete-stack functor, with coherent refinement equivalences; it does not assert uniqueness among all extensions.

This literal bridge is proved, but it is semantically trivial: every component gerbe is neutral and every Giraud class and hidden subgroup is zero.

The substantive bridge requested by the assessment fails exactly. AMB assigns
\[
\gamma_e(s)\in\check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0})
\]
to a chosen local section \(s\), using relative Čech cohomology of a presheaf; equivalently, it is a torsor class. This paper assigns a derived \(H^2\)-class for a sheaf band only to a global component of \(aS_e\). For strongly contextual models \((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), so the branch map has empty domain precisely where AMB can have nonzero classes. Therefore the Giraud class neither recovers nor refines AMB without an additional, presently absent degree-shifting construction.

**Transfer**

Only the support-level correspondence transfers functorially. Compatible supported families and global supported assignments are already the same set in the AB framework, so this paper’s `CompSec`/`Sec` gap collapses there. Probabilistic noncontextuality remains a separate distribution-extension problem.

The \(d(G)\le2\beta\), non-cyclic-\(p\)-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models. It remains a theorem about separately chosen bouquet sites, finite bands, two branches, and cocycle data. The canonical empirical-model lift has zero kernel.

**Clause (iv)**

[sec_branch_realization.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/sec_branch_realization.tex:109) now proves the degeneration internally: every generated cover of a nonempty slice object contains its identity; the empty cover forces value \(0\) at the strict initial object. Hence the abelian sheaf category is equivalent to a presheaf category on the nonempty slice, terminal evaluation is exact, and all higher slice cohomology vanishes. Ambient contractibility is used only to identify coefficient groups with \(A\), not to infer derived acyclicity.

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre; with $H^1$-vanishing this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf there. Hence gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice of local representatives. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a canonical Giraud class in $H^2$. For finite abelian bands this yields a homological evaluation map whose image controls a presentation-object visible-quotient invariant, while the character-blind case is exactly the pure $\operatorname{Ext}$ contribution. On fixed finite nerves with $H_1=0$ and $H_2\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, mixed realizations produce precisely the hidden subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements; on bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
+We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

**Literature**

No existing bridge from finite Abramsky–Brandenburger empirical models to banded realization stacks or gerbes was found in arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or zbMATH. Semantic Scholar’s final bulk searches returned zero results for `contextuality gerbe`, `empirical model gerbe`, and `banded gerbe contextuality`.

The closest results are materially different:

- Carù proves that AMB’s first cohomology classes classify torsors trivialized by the measurement cover.
- Barbosa–Kharoof–Okay construct fully faithful, empirical-model-compatible functors into bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios.
- Neither construction produces a sheaf-banded gerbe, a Giraud \(H^2\)-class, or this paper’s realization-stack extension. **Precise Result**

[sec_branch_contextuality.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/sec_branch_contextuality.tex:1) now treats finite no-signalling empirical models on the terminal augmentation of the finite context site. For context refinements whose context inclusion is continuous and satisfies support base change, it proves the pseudonatural assignment
\[
\mathfrak E_e^0=\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)
\]
with canonical zero band. After separately supplying an abelian sheaf \(\mathscr A\), it gives the split extension
\[
\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\mathscr A .
\]
“Canonical” means the choice-free composite of sheafification and the discrete-stack functor, with coherent refinement equivalences; it does not assert uniqueness among all extensions.

This literal bridge is proved, but it is semantically trivial: every component gerbe is neutral and every Giraud class and hidden subgroup is zero.

The substantive bridge requested by the assessment fails exactly. AMB assigns
\[
\gamma_e(s)\in\check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0})
\]
to a chosen local section \(s\), using relative Čech cohomology of a presheaf; equivalently, it is a torsor class. This paper assigns a derived \(H^2\)-class for a sheaf band only to a global component of \(aS_e\). For strongly contextual models \((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), so the branch map has empty domain precisely where AMB can have nonzero classes. Therefore the Giraud class neither recovers nor refines AMB without an additional, presently absent degree-shifting construction.

**Transfer**

Only the support-level correspondence transfers functorially. Compatible supported families and global supported assignments are already the same set in the AB framework, so this paper’s `CompSec`/`Sec` gap collapses there. Probabilistic noncontextuality remains a separate distribution-extension problem.

The \(d(G)\le2\beta\), non-cyclic-\(p\)-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models. It remains a theorem about separately chosen bouquet sites, finite bands, two branches, and cocycle data. The canonical empirical-model lift has zero kernel.

**Clause (iv)**

[sec_branch_realization.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_homological_visibility_gluing_obstructions_state_forcing_apal/sec_branch_realization.tex:109) now proves the degeneration internally: every generated cover of a nonempty slice object contains its identity; the empty cover forces value \(0\) at the strict initial object. Hence the abelian sheaf category is equivalent to a presheaf category on the nonempty slice, terminal evaluation is exact, and all higher slice cohomology vanishes. Ambient contractibility is used only to identify coefficient groups with \(A\), not to infer derived acyclicity.
